newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea MPs admit taking Hanbo money - prosecution.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea MPs admit taking Hanbo money - prosecution.

text.p: Four of the five members of the South Korean parliament questioned by state prosecutors on Saturday have admitted to taking money from the stricken Hanbo Group's founder, a prosecution official said on Sunday.
"Two of the four acknowledged their aides had taken 30-50 million won ($33,700-$56,100) and two others admitted taking themselves," the official told Reuters.
He said Lee Choong-jae of the splinter Democratic Party and Park Sung-vum of the ruling New Korea Party had admitted accepting 30 million won and 50 million won, respectively.
The prosecution is probing a loans-for-kickbacks scandal uncovered when Hanbo's flagship unit Hanbo Steel Co folded in January under $5.8 billion of debts.
The scandal revealed a web of corruption and influence-peddling involving top bankers and politicians.
Chung Tae-soo, the Hanbo founder on trial for bribing politicians and bankers in return for help in getting loans, last week told a parliamentary inquiry he had given money to leading politicians.
The official quoted the New Korea Party's Kim Deog-ryong and Park Chong-woong as saying their aides had taken 50 million won and an unspecified amount of money, respectively.
Kim Deog-ryong, a member of President Kim Young-sam's inner circle and one of nine tipped as the party's candidate in later this year's presidential polls, earlier denied taking money.
Lah Oh-yeon of the New Korea Party denied taking money, while Chung earlier said he had given 50 million won to Lah in 1992, the prosecution official said.
It was not clear whether any of those lawmakers who admitted taking money would face criminal charges.
All the five lawmakers had been released by early Sunday.
Meanwhile, the Yonhap Television News reported five more people, including a senior ruling party member of parliament, had been summoned to appear on Monday for questioning.

The prosecution official confirmed four people would appear on Monday, but declined to confirm summons for Kim Yoon-whan, a senior New Korea Party member and one of those tipped as the party's candidate in the presidential polls.
The prosecution plans to summon for questioning all the remainder of the 33 politicians named by Chung this week, the Yonhap Television News reported.
Separately, a parliamentary inquiry started last week and has heard evidence from Chung Tae-soo, top bankers and a close associate of President Kim.

Chung and his son Bo-keun, who was jailed in late March for embezzlement of company funds, will be in the spotlight on Monday when the younger Chung is due to testify before the parliamentary inquiry while his father stands trial.
